from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Vectors are directed segments from the origin.",
            "Visualize 2D vectors as simple arrows.",
            "Scaling and adding vectors creates linear combinations."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: The Vector Concept", lecture_lines)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 5], y_range=[-1, 5], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(axes)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        v1 = Vector(RIGHT + UP, color="#FF5733")
        self.place_at_grid(v1, "D3")
        self.play(Create(v1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        v_scaled = Vector(2 * (RIGHT + UP), color="#FF5733")
        self.place_at_grid(v_scaled, "D3")
        v_rotated = v_scaled.copy().rotate(PI/4)
        
        self.play(Transform(v1, v_scaled))
        self.play(Transform(v1, v_rotated))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#5733FF")
        v2 = Vector(RIGHT*2 + DOWN*0.5, color="#5733FF")
        self.place_at_grid(v2, "D3")
        
        res = Vector(v_rotated.get_end() + v2.get_end(), color="#33FF57")
        self.place_at_grid(res, "D3")
        
        self.play(Create(v2))
        self.play(Create(res))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Concept of Span: 'Reachability'", [
            "Span is the set of all reachable points.",
            "Think of it as area covered by vectors.",
            "Vectors define what space we can reach."
        ])

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Linear dependence means one vector is redundant.",
            "It adds no new dimensions to space.",
            "Dependent vectors lie on existing planes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Linear Dependence: The 'Redundant' Vector", lecture_lines)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "A basis is a minimal spanning set.",
            "It provides an efficient coordinate system.",
            "No redundancy, yet spans the space perfectly."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Bases: The Minimalist Framework", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup grid for visual
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GRAY}
        )
        # Using place_in_area to fit the grid
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.add(axes)

        # Basis vectors i and j
        i_vec = Vector(RIGHT, color=YELLOW)
        j_vec = Vector(UP, color=YELLOW)
        
        i_label = MathTex(r"\hat{i}", color=YELLOW)
        j_label = MathTex(r"\hat{j}", color=YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(i_vec), Create(j_vec))
        self.place_at_grid(i_label, 'D4')
        i_label.next_to(i_vec.get_end(), DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(j_label, 'D4')
        j_label.next_to(j_vec.get_end(), LEFT)
        self.play(Write(i_label), Write(j_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Grid lines representation
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        for k in range(-2, 3):
            line_h = Line(axes.c2p(-2, k), axes.c2p(2, k), stroke_width=1, color=BLUE_D)
            line_v = Line(axes.c2p(k, -2), axes.c2p(k, 2), stroke_width=1, color=BLUE_D)
            grid_lines.add(line_h, line_v)
        
        self.play(Create(grid_lines))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(axes.c2p(x, y), color=WHITE, radius=0.05) for x in range(-2, 3) for y in range(-2, 3)])
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", [
            "Linear combinations build up our spanning sets.", 
            "Redundancy creates linear dependence in vectors.", 
            "Bases are the minimal set for space."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Briefly summarize span concept with a recap animation.
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color=BLUE) for _ in range(5)])
        span_area = self.place_in_area(dots.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2), 'A1', 'B6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(span_area))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display linear dependence rule as a formula #FF00FF.
        dep_formula = MathTex(r"c_1v_1 + c_2v_2 = 0", color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(dep_formula, 'D3', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(dep_formula))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show a basis forming a complete coordinate system.
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 1], y_range=[-1, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'E1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Vector Spaces: Span, Dependence, and Bases

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Vector Concept
sections.content: Define a vector as a directed line segment from the origin. Visualize 2D vectors as arrows. Introduce 'Linear Combination' as scaling and adding arrows together.
sections.example: Imagine a robot arm moving in a 2D plane: scaling two basic motor inputs (v1, v2) to reach any coordinate (x, y).

sections.title: The Concept of Span: 'Reachability'
sections.content: Define Span as the set of all possible points reachable by taking linear combinations of a set of vectors. Visualize this as the 'shadow' or 'area' cast by the vectors.
sections.example: Two non-parallel vectors in 2D 'span' the entire plane; one vector only spans a single line.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: The 'Redundant' Vector
sections.content: Explain Linear Dependence: A set is dependent if one vector can be expressed as a combination of others (i.e., it doesn't add 'new' dimensions). Visualize this as a third vector lying flat on the plane formed by the first two.
sections.example: If you have three people pulling a wagon in the same direction, the third person is 'linearly dependent'—their effort doesn't change the path.

sections.title: Bases: The Minimalist Framework
sections.content: Define a Basis as the 'Goldilocks' set: enough vectors to span the space, but no redundancy (linearly independent). This acts as a coordinate system for the space.
sections.example: The standard basis vectors i=(1,0) and j=(0,1) are the most efficient 'map' for a 2D grid.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap the logical progression: Linear Combinations build Span; too many vectors create Dependence; the minimal set required to span is a Basis.
sections.example: Think of a basis as the 'keys' on a piano: they are independent notes that, when combined, can span the entire musical range of the instrument.
